newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS - LVMH stock up, market awaits UK groups' reply.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - LVMH stock up, market awaits UK groups' reply.

text.p: Shares in LVMH rose on Wednesday as the market awaited a response from British groups Guinness and Grand Metropolitan to LVMH chairman Bernard Arnault's proposal for a three-way drinks merger.

Several share analysts said they expected the British groups, which announced their own plans to merge in May, to turn LVMH down but leave the door open to negotiations over the terms for the creation of a group blending their drinks businesses.
LVMH's stock was up 3.98 percent at 1,621 francs at 1030 GMT, outperforming the Paris bourse as a whole, which was up 2.9 percent.
"I think Arnault has the upper hand and the market's pricing that in. Guinness and Grand Met are on the defensive," a London-based analyst said.
"Arnault's coming to London tomorrow to see large institutional investors in Guinness and GrandMet."

The LVMH boss is expected to argue that a three-way drinks group would create more shareholder value than the 24 billion pound ($40.3 billion) fast food, canned goods, spirits and beer conglomerate planned by the British companies.
Arnault has signalled in recent days that he is flexible on what stake he envisages for LVMH in the new group.
LVMH initially said its 66 percent Moet Hennessy stake and its holdings in Guinness and GrandMet would entitle it to around 35 percent.
But the group is willing to discuss valuations. Analysts say the British companies have said LVMH's holdings would entitle it to 25 percent and they expect a compromise at around 30 percent.
Brokers said the LVMH stock rise was also a rebound from recent profit-taking on nervousness over the high-stakes brawl between LVMH, its one-time ally Guinness and GrandMet.
The ties between Guinness and LVMH were severed on Wednesday as the Guinness board said it unanimously accepted Arnault's resignation. Guinness chairman Tony Greener quit LVMH's board in May.

LVMH's stock had fallen 0.3 percent on Tuesday, underperforming the market, after LVMH roughly doubled its stake in GrandMet to more than 10 percent. LVMH confirmed that it bought shares in Grand Met and sold stock in Guinness.
Analysts said the market was also waiting to learn the levels of LVMH's holdings in the two groups, which should be disclosed after being registered with Britain's Takeover Panel.
Paris brokerage Ferri said market sources estimate LVMH now holds 10 to 12 percent of GrandMet.

"It has thus spent 4.7 billion francs. The money would come from Guinness sales -- we estimate four percent of Guinness may have been sold. Bernard Arnault's strategy is thus to hold 10 percent of Guinness and 10 percent of GrandMet, a level which permits him to call extraordinary general meetings under British law," it said in its daily stock comment.

Several market players say the market is growing increasingly confident that Arnault would prevail if he brought his case directly to the holders of the widely dispersed capital of the British groups.

LVMH, the largest shareholder in both Guinness and GrandMet, has opposed their merger, which risks marginalising its Moet Hennessy drinks business and locking up part of the group's capital in a subsidiary of the new merged group.
-- Christine Tierney, Paris Newsroom, +33 1 4221 5452 ($ = 0.595 British Pounds)
